lessons.title: Observing properties of materials
lessons.description: Compare materials by observable properties and choose suitable uses.
lessons.content: Materials can be compared by properties such as hardness, flexibility, transparency and ability to absorb water. A property helps explain why a material is suitable for a particular use. Careful observation describes what is seen without guessing.
learning_objectives: Describe common observable properties of materials.
Choose a material for a use by matching its properties to the task.
prerequisites: Use senses safely to observe classroom objects.

explanation_sections.title: Describe what you observe
explanation_sections.body: A transparent material lets much light pass through so objects can be seen clearly. A flexible material bends without breaking easily. Hardness describes resistance to scratching or denting. State the observation and the test used.

explanation_sections.title: Match properties to purpose
explanation_sections.body: A clear window needs a transparent material; a raincoat needs a material that resists water. One material may be useful for several reasons. Recap: identify the job, compare relevant properties and explain your choice.

worked_examples.prompt: Choose between clear glass and opaque wood for a classroom window, if the aim is to let in light and see outside.
worked_examples.reasoning: Its transparency allows light through and lets people see objects outside.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which property describes a material that lets you see objects clearly through it?
questions.explanation: Transparent materials allow light through so objects can be seen clearly.

questions.prompt: Which property is most useful when selecting cloth to soak up a small spill?
questions.explanation: An absorbent material takes in liquid and is useful for soaking up a spill.

questions.prompt: What makes a material suitable for a raincoat?
questions.explanation: A raincoat should help keep water from reaching the clothes underneath.

lessons.title: Solids, liquids and gases
lessons.description: Compare the shape and volume of common states of matter.
lessons.content: Matter is commonly described as solid, liquid or gas. A solid keeps its shape and volume; a liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container; a gas spreads to fill the available space.
learning_objectives: Classify familiar substances by state at room conditions.
Compare how solids, liquids and gases behave in containers.
prerequisites: Observe water, ice and air in safe everyday situations.

explanation_sections.title: Shape and volume
explanation_sections.body: A solid has a fixed shape and volume. A liquid flows and changes shape to fit the container, while its amount has a fixed volume. A gas spreads out and fills the available space.

explanation_sections.title: Changes of state
explanation_sections.body: Heating can melt a solid into a liquid and, with further heating, change a liquid to a gas. Cooling can reverse these changes. Recap: compare whether a substance keeps its shape and whether it fills its container.

worked_examples.prompt: Water is poured from a narrow bottle into a wide bowl. What changes and what stays the same?
worked_examples.solution: Its shape changes to fit the bowl; the amount of water stays the same if none is spilled.
worked_examples.reasoning: A liquid takes its container's shape while retaining its volume.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which state of matter keeps its own shape and volume?
questions.explanation: A solid has a fixed shape and volume.

questions.prompt: What does a liquid do when poured into a different container?
options: Takes the new container's shape but keeps its volume.
Fills all the space like a gas.
questions.correct_answer: Takes the new container's shape but keeps its volume.
questions.explanation: Liquids flow to take the container's shape but have a fixed volume.

questions.prompt: Which state spreads to fill all available space in a closed container?
questions.explanation: A gas spreads out to occupy the available space in its container.

lessons.title: Separating simple mixtures
lessons.description: Select a suitable physical method to separate components of a mixture.
lessons.content: A mixture contains two or more substances together without forming a new substance. Some mixtures can be separated using differences in particle size, magnetic properties or whether a substance dissolves in water.
learning_objectives: Recognise that mixtures can contain visible different materials.
Choose a simple separation method for a mixture.

explanation_sections.title: Match method to property
explanation_sections.body: A sieve separates larger solid pieces from smaller ones. A magnet can remove magnetic material from a mixture. Filtering can separate an insoluble solid from a liquid by trapping solid particles in filter material.

explanation_sections.title: Use safe, fair tests
explanation_sections.body: Choose a method based on a property that differs between the components. Do not taste unknown mixtures or use heat without adult supervision. Recap: observe the mixture, identify a useful difference and select a safe method.

worked_examples.prompt: How can small stones be separated from dry sand when the stones are larger?
worked_examples.solution: Pass the mixture through a suitable sieve.
worked_examples.reasoning: The sieve openings allow sand through while retaining larger stones.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which method can separate an insoluble solid from water?
questions.explanation: A filter traps insoluble solid particles while liquid passes through.

questions.prompt: A mixture contains iron filings and sand. Which tool can help remove the iron?
questions.explanation: Iron is attracted to a magnet, while ordinary sand is not.

questions.prompt: What property makes a sieve useful for separating stones from sand?
options: The components have different particle sizes.
questions.correct_answer: The components have different particle sizes.
questions.explanation: A sieve separates solid pieces according to whether they fit through its openings.
